Herlev Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd. (Herlev Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology) is a healthcare facility evaluated in the Danish quality program for inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), as documented in the DANIBD 2024 report [^src1]. The facility's performance is tracked across key clinical quality indicators designed to monitor evidence-based care and standardize treatment protocols [^src1].

Specifically, the department's data is featured in the evaluations for Indicator 4 and Indicator 5 [^src1]. Indicator 4 measures the rate of DEXA scans for patients undergoing steroid treatment, while Indicator 5 tracks fecal calprotectin measurements for patients receiving BMSL (biological and small molecule) therapy [^src1]. According to the 2024 report, Herlev Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd. achieved a 42% compliance rate for DEXA scanning, completing 41 out of 97 eligible scans [^src1]. For fecal calprotectin measurements, the department recorded a 69% compliance rate, with 581 measurements taken out of 846 eligible instances [^src1].

These figures are part of a broader narrative regarding quality development in Danish IBD care. The report notes a severe lack of fulfillment of the 80% development target for both indicators across various regions and departments [^src1]. Herlev's performance underscores the systemic challenges and the ongoing need for improved coordination of quality metrics across different treatment modalities in IBD management [^src1].
